title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Public Security on the Issue of Maritime Court Judges and Others Boarding Foreign Ships for Handling Maritime Cases

articles.content_en:
I. When adjudicators, enforcement personnel, and judicial police of a maritime court need to board a foreign vessel in the course of handling a case, they shall board the vessel with the "Certificate for Execution of Official Duties" issued by the president of the maritime court and wearing the court uniform as prescribed by the state; interpreters and expert evaluation personnel accompanying the case-handling personnel shall board the vessel with the notice of the maritime court. The maritime court shall notify the frontier inspection station of the boarding time and number of persons in advance.
The "Certificate for Execution of Official Duties" shall be used within its validity period.
II. When a maritime court boards a foreign vessel at an inland river port open to foreign vessels to handle a case, the provisions above shall be followed mutatis mutandis.

III. The case-handling personnel, interpreters, and expert evaluation personnel of the maritime court who board a foreign vessel must strictly comply with the "Rules for Personnel Boarding Foreign Vessels" approved by Document No. 99 (1981) of the State Council.
It is hereby notified, and compliance is required.
Appendix: Style of the Certificate for Execution of Official Duties of Maritime Court (omitted)
